en: The Noble Sūtra of the One Hundred and Fifty Verses on the Perfection of Wisdom in Non-duality.
Homage to the Blessed Noble Perfection of Wisdom!
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty, as well as with many Brahmās, Śakras, world-protectors, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and male and female lay devotees.
Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti:
"Subhūti, whoever wishes to train in the path of the śrāvakas must listen to, take up, bear in mind, recite, teach, and master this very perfection of wisdom.
Herein, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, endowed with skill in means, should apply himself to the realization of all the qualities of a Buddha through this very perfection of wisdom."
For what reason?
Because herein, in this perfection of wisdom, all the qualities of a Buddha are taught in detail;
it is therein that a bodhisattva must train.

"Subhūti, whatever wholesome dharmas there are—whether they be factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika*), dharmas of a śrāvaka, dharmas of a pratyekabuddha, dharmas of a bodhisattva, or dharmas of a Buddha—all those factors conducive to enlightenment, dharmas of a śrāvaka, dharmas of a pratyekabuddha, and dharmas of a bodhisattva are included within, have entered into, and reach their synthesis and convergence in this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, it is just as follows: the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*), the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*), the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*), and the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)."

Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate truth, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, emptiness of that which is without beginning or end,
emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of all phenomena, emptiness of specific characteristics, and emptiness of non-apprehension.
The emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
the four foundations of mindfulness;
the four right efforts.
The four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, and the five powers.
The seven factors of enlightenment;
the noble eightfold path.
The four meditative absorptions, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
The eight liberations,
the nine successive meditative attainments,
and all the gateways of dhāraṇī.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges.
Great loving-kindness, great compassion,
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and omniscience.

"Subhūti, these very wholesome dharmas—the factors conducive to awakening, the dharmas of the śrāvakas, and the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas—are contained within this perfection of wisdom; they have entered into it and proceed toward its inclusion and convergence. Subhūti said: "Aho! Aho!"
Truly, this perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom,

insofar as the wholesome dharmas— the factors conducive to enlightenment, the dharmas of the śrāvakas, the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of the buddhas—
are all contained within it, have entered into it, and go toward its inclusion and convergence.
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, it is because of its absolute liberation that it is called the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti said: "Aho! Aho! Truly, this perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom!"
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, it is because of its absolute purity that the perfection of wisdom is such.
Subhūti said: "Aho! Aho!
Indeed, Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom!"
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, because it is absolutely pure, the perfection of wisdom is therefore, Subhūti, like space.
Subhūti said: "Aho! Aho!"
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed difficult to fathom for one who is not diligent.
The Blessed One said: "It is just as you say.
This perfection of wisdom is difficult to resolve with faith by one who is not diligent, whose roots of virtue are meager, and who is dull-witted; yet it is not so for Subhūti, who is undisturbed."

Indeed not, Subhūti, for one who is accompanied by a bad friend, who belongs to the faction of bad friends, who is joined with a multitude of bad friends, who is possessed of the undertaking of a bad friend,

who is a destroyer of the true Dharma, who is a mere beginner, who is utterly unqualified, who is by nature one who does not inquire, who is conducive to lack of wisdom, who is indolent, of inferior character, lacking resolve in wholesome dharmas, and not applying himself to them. It is for such a person, Subhūti, that [this would not be possible].
The perfection of wisdom is said to be difficult to resolve with faith.

Furthermore, Subhūti, any son of good family or daughter of good family who speaks, maintains, recites, teaches, and masters this profound perfection of wisdom will [be sustained] by the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present.
"Bodhisattvas shall uphold the enlightenment of the Buddhas.
Therefore, Subhūti, monks who desire unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment should, with resolute intention, take up this perfection of wisdom and supernormal knowledge.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. And the entire assembly, including the gods, rejoiced, delighting in what the Blessed One had said.
The *Advayaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī Sūtra* is completed. // 0 //
